chapter: His own groups, compositions and friends
title: Charles Colin's help after the move to New York
summary: When Baker moved to New York in 1977-78, Charles Colin paid him to write books, gave him studio space and took him under his wing.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Benefactor, really good friend, again. When I went to – moved to New York in 1977 or whenever it was, Charles Colin . . .

. . . Charles Colin just really took me under [his] wing – and published – paid me to write books that he didn’t need, but he paid me to write them – books of duets, books of other things, and took me under his wing. He provided me [with] a studio to use, a place to store materials, and even bought me a corduroy suit one Christmas.
